title: Reporting what has been done
grammar: Present Perfect passivo (has / have been + particípio)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Present Perfect passivo (has / have been + particípio) para relatar o que já foi feito sem dizer quem fez. Em Qualidade e PCP da Delta Ducon, é assim que você atualiza o status de uma inspeção, diz que os relatórios já foram aprovados e confirma que as não conformidades já foram encerradas.
intro: In quality work, we report what has been done, not who did it. The scrubber has been inspected. The reports have been approved. The focus is on the result.
Today we practise the present perfect passive: has or have been plus the past participle. It is the natural language of inspection records and audit updates at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Welcome back. This week the scrubbers have been inspected and the reports have been approved by the auditor. Every non-conformity has been closed. In this lesson you will learn to say what has been done, using has and have been plus the past participle.
vocab: The dust collector has been inspected this week.
The inspection report has been approved by the auditor.
The worn filter bags have been replaced.
The quality procedures have been updated recently.
All the non-conformities have been closed.
The documents have been submitted to the client.
practice: The scrubber has been ______ before delivery.
inspected
The final report has been ______ by the manager.
approved
The damaged filter bags have been ______.
replaced
The ISO 9001 procedures have been ______ this year.
updated
Every non-conformity has been ______ after the audit.
closed
The test results have been ______ to the client.
submitted
The welds have been ______ on each panel.
inspected
The new checklist has been ______ by the quality team.
approved

audio.title: This week's quality update
audio.text: This has been a productive week for the quality team. All the dust collectors have been inspected and the results have been recorded in the system. The worn filter bags have been replaced and the scrubber has been tested at the factory. Every non-conformity from the last audit has been closed. The inspection reports have been approved by the auditor and have been submitted to the client. Nothing has been shipped before it has been fully checked.

readAloud: The dust collector has been inspected this week.
The reports have been approved by the auditor.
The worn filter bags have been replaced.
All the non-conformities have been closed.
The documents have been submitted to the client.
fill: The scrubber has been ___ before delivery. (inspect)
The reports have been ___ by the auditor. (approve)
The procedures have been ___ this year. (update)
The results have been ___ to the client. (submit)
The defect has been ___ during the inspection. (find)
The samples have been ___ in the lab. (measure)
qa: Has the scrubber been inspected?
Yes, it has been inspected before delivery.
Have the filter bags been replaced?
Yes, they have been replaced this week.
Has the report been approved?
Yes, it has been approved by the auditor.
Have all the non-conformities been closed?
Yes, they have all been closed.
Has the documentation been submitted to the client?
Yes, it has been submitted.
sentences: The dust collector has been inspected this week.
The reports have been approved by the auditor.
The worn filter bags have been replaced.
The ISO 9001 procedures have been updated recently.
All the non-conformities have been closed.
The test results have been submitted to the client.
The scrubber has been tested at the factory.
The corrective actions have been completed on time.
grammarPoint: Present Perfect passivo: has / have been + particípio passado. Usamos para dizer que algo já foi feito, sem focar em quem fez. The report has been approved. — O relatório já foi aprovado. The parts have been inspected. — As peças já foram inspecionadas. Use 'has been' com singular e 'have been' com plural.
deepDive: A estrutura tem três partes: has/have + been + particípio. O 'been' nunca muda; só o auxiliar concorda com o sujeito (has para singular, have para plural). É muito usada em status de qualidade e atas: informa o resultado atual de uma ação passada. Palavras como 'already', 'just' e 'not yet' combinam bem: The audit has just been closed.
examples: The report has been approved.
O relatório já foi aprovado.
The filter bags have been replaced.
As mangas do filtro já foram substituídas.
The scrubber has been inspected.
O lavador de gases já foi inspecionado.
The procedures have been updated.
Os procedimentos já foram atualizados.
The non-conformity has been closed.
A não conformidade já foi encerrada.
The documents have been submitted.
Os documentos já foram enviados.
The results have been recorded in the system.
Os resultados já foram registrados no sistema.
Nothing has been shipped without approval.
Nada foi expedido sem aprovação.
mistakes: The report has been approve.
The report has been approved.
Depois de 'has been' vem o particípio (approved).
The parts has been inspected.
The parts have been inspected.
Com plural (parts) usamos have been.
The scrubber have been tested.
The scrubber has been tested.
Com singular (scrubber) usamos has been.
The filters have been replace.
The filters have been replaced.
Falta o particípio: replaced.
The report has approved.
The report has been approved.
Na passiva não pode faltar 'been': has been approved.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now report what has been inspected, approved and closed — the exact language of a quality status update.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você sabe relatar o que já foi inspecionado, aprovado e encerrado — a linguagem exata de um status de qualidade.

title: Rules that never change
grammar: Zero Conditional (if + presente, presente) — regras de processo
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Zero Conditional (if + presente, presente) para descrever regras de processo que são sempre verdadeiras. Em Qualidade e PCP da Delta Ducon, é assim que você explica a lógica de segurança e os critérios de inspeção: se a pressão sobe, a válvula abre; se uma amostra reprova, o lote é rejeitado.
intro: Some things in a process are always true. If the pressure rises, the valve opens. If a sample fails, we reject the batch. There is no doubt about the result.
Today we practise the zero conditional: if plus present, present. It is how we describe fixed process rules and safety logic at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: In our processes, some things are always true. If the pressure rises, the valve opens. If a sample fails the test, we reject the batch. Today you will learn the zero conditional, which we use for process rules that never change.
vocab: If the sensors detect a leak, the system stops.
If the pressure is too high, it triggers the alarm.
If the emission exceeds the limit, we stop the line.
If a sample fails, the inspector rejects the batch.
If a defect appears, the procedure requires a report.
If the temperature rises too much, the valve shuts.
practice: If the sensors ______ a leak, the system stops.
detect
If the readings are too high, they ______ the alarm.
trigger
If the emissions ______ the limit, we stop the line.
exceed
If a sample fails, the inspectors ______ the batch.
reject
If a defect appears, the procedures ______ a report.
require
If the valves ______, the gas flow drops.
shut
If we ______ a leak early, we avoid downtime.
detect
If the operators ______ the limit, the line stops.
exceed

audio.title: How our safety logic works
audio.text: Our systems follow simple rules that never change. If the pressure rises above the limit, the safety valve opens. If a sensor detects a leak, the alarm sounds and the line stops. If a sample fails the inspection, we reject the whole batch. If the emission exceeds the threshold, the process shuts down automatically. If we follow the procedure, the equipment stays under control. These are zero conditional rules, and they are always true.

readAloud: If the pressure rises, the valve opens.
If a sample fails the test, we reject the batch.
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stops.
If the sensor detects a leak, the alarm sounds.
If we follow the procedure, the process stays under control.
fill: If the pressure rises, the valve ___ automatically. (open)
If a sample fails, the inspector ___ the batch. (reject)
If the emission ___ the limit, the line stops. (exceed)
If the sensor ___ smoke, the alarm sounds. (detect)
If the temperature rises, the fan ___ faster. (run)
If we ___ the procedure, the process stays stable. (follow)
If the filter ___, the pressure drops. (clog)
If defects ___, the system opens a non-conformity. (appear)
qa: What happens if the pressure rises too much?
If the pressure rises too much, the valve opens.
What do you do if a sample fails the test?
If a sample fails, we reject the batch.
What happens if the emission exceeds the limit?
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stops.
What happens if the sensor detects a leak?
If the sensor detects a leak, the alarm sounds.
What happens if you follow the procedure?
If we follow the procedure, the process stays under control.

a.label: regra de processo (if + presente, presente)
a.placeholder: If the pressure rises, the valve opens

b.label: resultado no presente
b.placeholder: The alarm sounds if the sensor detects smoke

sentences: If the pressure rises, the valve opens automatically.
If a sample fails the test, we reject the batch.
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stops.
If the sensor detects a leak, the alarm sounds.
If the temperature rises, the fan runs faster.
If we follow the procedure, the process stays under control.
If a defect appears, the system opens a non-conformity.
If the filter clogs, the pressure drops.
grammarPoint: Zero Conditional: if + presente simples, presente simples. Usamos para regras e verdades que são sempre certas. If the pressure rises, the valve opens. — Se a pressão sobe, a válvula abre. If a sample fails, we reject it. — Se uma amostra reprova, nós a rejeitamos. As duas partes ficam no presente.
deepDive: No zero conditional o resultado é automático e sempre igual, por isso não usa 'will' (isso seria First Conditional, para o futuro). Na terceira pessoa (the sensor, the valve) o verbo leva -s: detects, opens. Você pode trocar 'if' por 'when' com o mesmo sentido de regra: When the pressure rises, the valve opens.
examples: If the pressure rises, the valve opens.
Se a pressão sobe, a válvula abre.
If a sample fails, we reject the batch.
Se uma amostra reprova, rejeitamos o lote.
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stops.
Se a emissão ultrapassa o limite, a linha para.
If the sensor detects a leak, the alarm sounds.
Se o sensor detecta um vazamento, o alarme dispara.
If the filter clogs, the pressure drops.
Se o filtro entope, a pressão cai.
If we follow the procedure, quality stays stable.
Se seguimos o procedimento, a qualidade se mantém estável.
If a defect appears, the system opens a non-conformity.
Se um defeito aparece, o sistema abre uma não conformidade.
When the temperature rises, the fan runs faster.
Quando a temperatura sobe, o ventilador gira mais rápido.
mistakes: If the pressure rises, the valve will open.
If the pressure rises, the valve opens.
Regra sempre verdadeira usa presente, não will (will seria First Conditional).
If the sensor detect smoke, the alarm sounds.
If the sensor detects smoke, the alarm sounds.
Terceira pessoa (the sensor) leva -s: detects.
If a sample will fail, we reject it.
If a sample fails, we reject it.
Depois de if usamos o presente, não will.
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stop.
If the emission exceeds the limit, the line stops.
A linha (singular) leva -s: stops.
If the pressure rises the valve opens.
If the pressure rises, the valve opens.
Falta a vírgula depois da oração com if.
quick: If the pressure rises, the valve ___. (open)
If a sample fails, we ___ it. (reject)
If the emission ___ the limit, the line stops. (exceed)
If the sensor ___ smoke, the alarm sounds. (detect)
If the filter ___, the pressure drops. (clog)

celebrate.en: Great job. You can now explain the fixed rules of a process — the logic behind every safety system and inspection criterion.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você sabe explicar as regras fixas de um processo — a lógica por trás de todo sistema de segurança e critério de inspeção.

title: Getting the job done by others
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o causativo (have / get something done) para dizer que alguém faz um serviço para você. Em Qualidade e PCP da Delta Ducon, é assim que você fala das inspeções, calibrações e auditorias que empresas externas realizam nos seus equipamentos e no seu sistema ISO 9001.
intro: We do not carry out every task ourselves. We arrange for other companies to inspect, calibrate or repair our equipment.
Today we practise the causative, have and get something done. It lets you say that someone does a service for us at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: At Delta Ducon we do not do everything ourselves. We have the scrubbers inspected by a certified body, and we get the sensors calibrated every year. Today you will learn the causative, have and get something done, to say that someone does a job for us.
vocab: We have the scrubbers inspected by a certified body.
We get the sensors calibrated every year.
We had the fan repaired last week.
We get our process certified under ISO 9001.
We have our system audited by an external body.
We get the equipment serviced regularly.
practice: We have the scrubbers ______ by a certified body.
inspected
We get the sensors ______ every year.
calibrated
We had the damaged fan ______ last week.
repaired
We get our quality system ______ under ISO 9001.
certified
We have our processes ______ by an external body.
audited
We get the equipment ______ every six months.
serviced
We had the filter bags ______ before the restart.
inspected
We have the new supplier ______ before approval.
audited

audio.title: Services we arrange
audio.text: At Delta Ducon we manage quality, but we do not do every job in house. We have the scrubbers inspected by a certified body twice a year. We get the sensors calibrated so the readings are always accurate. Last month we had the main fan repaired by the supplier after a failure. We also get our quality system audited under ISO 9001 by an external company. By having these services done by experts, we keep our equipment reliable and our certificates valid.

readAloud: We have the scrubbers inspected by a certified body.
We get the sensors calibrated every year.
We had the fan repaired last week.
We get our system certified under ISO 9001.
We have the equipment serviced regularly.
fill: We have the scrubbers ___ by a certified body. (inspect)
We get the sensors ___ every year. (calibrate)
We had the fan ___ last week. (repair)
We get the process ___ under ISO 9001. (certify)
We have our system ___ by an external body. (audit)
We get the equipment ___ every six months. (service)
We had the filter bags ___ before the restart. (replace)
We have the documents ___ before the meeting. (review)
qa: Do you inspect the scrubbers yourselves?
No, we have them inspected by a certified body.
How often do you calibrate the sensors?
We get them calibrated every year.
Did you repair the fan?
We had it repaired last week.
Who certifies your quality system?
We get it certified under ISO 9001 by an external body.
How do you keep the equipment reliable?
We have it serviced regularly.
sentences: We have the scrubbers inspected by a certified body.
We get the sensors calibrated every year.
We had the damaged fan repaired last week.
We get our quality system certified under ISO 9001.
We have our processes audited by an external body.
We get the equipment serviced every six months.
We had the filter bags replaced before the restart.
We have the documents reviewed before delivery.
grammarPoint: Causativo have / get something done: sujeito + have/get + objeto + particípio. Significa que outra pessoa faz o serviço para você. We have the scrubber inspected. — Mandamos inspecionar o scrubber. We get the sensors calibrated. — Mandamos calibrar os sensores. 'Get' é um pouco mais informal que 'have'.
deepDive: A ordem é sempre objeto ANTES do particípio: have the fan repaired (não 'have repaired the fan', que muda o sentido). No passado use had / got: We had the fan repaired. Para dizer quem fez, use 'by': inspected by a certified body. É diferente da passiva simples porque você organiza/paga pelo serviço.
examples: We have the scrubbers inspected.
Mandamos inspecionar os scrubbers.
We get the sensors calibrated every year.
Mandamos calibrar os sensores todo ano.
We had the fan repaired last week.
Mandamos consertar o ventilador semana passada.
We get our process certified under ISO 9001.
Mandamos certificar nosso processo pela ISO 9001.
We have our system audited externally.
Temos nosso sistema auditado externamente.
We got the equipment serviced yesterday.
Mandamos fazer a manutenção do equipamento ontem.
The client has the report reviewed before delivery.
O cliente manda revisar o relatório antes da entrega.
We need to get the filter replaced.
Precisamos mandar substituir o filtro.
mistakes: We have inspected the scrubbers by a third party.
We have the scrubbers inspected by a third party.
No causativo o objeto vem antes do particípio: have the scrubbers inspected.
We get calibrated the sensors.
We get the sensors calibrated.
A ordem é get + objeto + particípio.
We had repaired the fan by a supplier.
We had the fan repaired by a supplier.
Causativo: had + objeto + particípio (repaired).
We have the system audit every year.
We have the system audited every year.
Depois do objeto vem o particípio: audited.
We get certify our process.
We get our process certified.
Ordem: get + objeto + particípio (certified).

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now say that a service is done for you — how quality teams talk about external inspections, calibrations and audits.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você sabe dizer que um serviço é feito para você — como as equipes de qualidade falam de inspeções, calibrações e auditorias externas.

title: Adding extra detail
grammar: Orações relativas não-restritivas (…, which / whose / where …)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender as orações relativas não-restritivas (…, which / whose / where …) para acrescentar informação extra sobre um equipamento, um lugar ou uma pessoa. Em Qualidade e PCP da Delta Ducon, isso deixa suas descrições de plantas, fornecedores e sistemas mais ricas e naturais em inglês.
intro: When we describe our plant, we often add extra information about a machine, a place or a person. The baghouse, which filters the dust, is huge.
Today we practise non-restrictive relative clauses with which, who, where and whose, always between commas, to add that extra detail at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Let me tell you about our plant. The baghouse, which filters the dust, is very large. The auditor, who visited us last week, approved our process. Today you will learn to add extra information with which, who, where and whose.
vocab: The baghouse, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
Our main supplier, whose quality is high, is in São Paulo.
The Diadema plant, where we assemble the units, is large.
The auditor, who visited us last week, approved the process.
The scrubber, which cleans the gas, was installed in June.
The batch, which failed the test, was rejected.
practice: The ______, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
baghouse
Our main ______, whose quality is high, is in São Paulo.
supplier
The Diadema ______, where we assemble the units, is large.
plant
The ______, who visited us last week, approved the process.
auditor
The ______, which cleans the gas, was installed in June.
scrubber
The ______, which failed the test, was rejected.
batch
The ______, who designed the system, works in Diadema.
auditor
The ______, which removes the dust from the air, has 200 filter bags.
baghouse

audio.title: A tour of the plant
audio.text: Welcome to our Diadema plant, where most of our equipment is assembled. The baghouse, which removes the dust from the gas, is the largest unit in the workshop. Our main supplier, whose filter bags we use in every project, has never let us down. The auditor, who visited us last week, checked every record and approved the process. The scrubber, which was installed in June, is already running well. This is a place where quality comes first.

readAloud: The baghouse, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
Our main supplier, whose quality is high, is in São Paulo.
The Diadema plant, where we assemble the units, is large.
The auditor, who visited us last week, approved the process.
The scrubber, which cleans the gas, was installed in June.
fill: The baghouse, ___ filters the dust, needs cleaning. (coisa)
The auditor, ___ visited us last week, approved the report. (pessoa)
The Diadema plant, ___ we assemble the units, is large. (lugar)
Our supplier, ___ quality is high, is reliable. (posse)
The scrubber, ___ cleans the gas, was installed in June. (coisa)
The engineer, ___ designed the system, works in Diadema. (pessoa)
The workshop, ___ the panels are welded, is very clean. (lugar)
The batch, ___ failed the test, was rejected. (coisa)
qa: What does the baghouse do?
The baghouse, which filters the dust, protects the environment.
Who approved the report?
The auditor, who visited us last week, approved it.
Where do you assemble the units?
At the Diadema plant, where we have our main workshop.
Is your supplier reliable?
Yes, our supplier, whose quality is high, is very reliable.
What happened to the batch?
The batch, which failed the test, was rejected.

a.label: info extra com , which
a.placeholder: The scrubber, which cleans the gas, is new

b.label: , who / , where / , whose
b.placeholder: The auditor, who visited us, approved it

sentences: The baghouse, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
Our main supplier, whose quality is high, is in São Paulo.
The Diadema plant, where we assemble the units, is very large.
The auditor, who visited us last week, approved the process.
The scrubber, which cleans the gas, was installed in June.
The batch, which failed the inspection, was rejected.
The engineer, who designed the system, works in Diadema.
The workshop, where the panels are welded, is very clean.
grammarPoint: Orações relativas não-restritivas dão informação EXTRA (não essencial) e vão entre vírgulas. Use which para coisas, who para pessoas, where para lugares e whose para posse. The scrubber, which cleans the gas, is new. — O scrubber, que limpa o gás, é novo. The auditor, who visited us, approved it. — O auditor, que nos visitou, aprovou.
deepDive: Com vírgulas, a informação é um extra: se você tirar a oração, a frase ainda faz sentido. Nunca use 'that' nas não-restritivas — só which/who/where/whose. Não confunda whose (posse) com who's (= who is). O 'which' também pode se referir à frase inteira: The audit passed, which pleased the client.
examples: The baghouse, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
O filtro de mangas, que filtra a poeira, precisa de limpeza.
The auditor, who visited us, approved the report.
O auditor, que nos visitou, aprovou o relatório.
The Diadema plant, where we assemble the units, is large.
A planta de Diadema, onde montamos as unidades, é grande.
Our supplier, whose quality is high, never fails.
Nosso fornecedor, cuja qualidade é alta, nunca falha.
The scrubber, which cleans the gas, was installed in June.
O scrubber, que limpa o gás, foi instalado em junho.
The batch, which failed the test, was rejected.
O lote, que reprovou no teste, foi rejeitado.
The report, which took two days, is now ready.
O relatório, que levou dois dias, está pronto agora.
The engineer, who designed the system, is very experienced.
O engenheiro, que projetou o sistema, é muito experiente.
mistakes: The scrubber that cleans the gas, is new.
The scrubber, which cleans the gas, is new.
Em oração não-restritiva usamos which (com vírgulas), não that.
The auditor, which visited us, approved it.
The auditor, who visited us, approved it.
Para pessoas usamos who, não which.
The plant, which we assemble the units, is large.
The plant, where we assemble the units, is large.
Para lugar usamos where.
The supplier, who's quality is high, is reliable.
The supplier, whose quality is high, is reliable.
Posse é whose, não who's (= who is).
The baghouse which filters the dust needs cleaning.
The baghouse, which filters the dust, needs cleaning.
A informação extra vai entre vírgulas.
quick: The scrubber, ___ cleans the gas, is new. (coisa)
The auditor, ___ visited us, approved it. (pessoa)
The plant, ___ we assemble the units, is large. (lugar)
The supplier, ___ quality is high, is reliable. (posse)
The batch, ___ failed the test, was rejected. (coisa)

celebrate.en: Great work. You can now add extra detail smoothly — describing plants, suppliers and systems the way a native speaker would.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você sabe acrescentar detalhes com naturalidade — descrevendo plantas, fornecedores e sistemas como um nativo faria.

title: Showing contrast in reports
grammar: Contraste — although / even though / despite / in spite of
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a mostrar contraste com although, even though, despite e in spite of. Em Qualidade e PCP da Delta Ducon, isso é essencial para relatar resultados equilibrados: apesar de um atraso ou de uma não conformidade, a entrega foi cumprida e a qualidade se manteve alta.
intro: Quality reports are full of contrasts: a problem on one side, a good result on the other. Although we found a defect, we met the deadline.
Today we practise four ways to show contrast: although, even though, despite and in spite of. Two link clauses, and two link nouns.
introAudio: Reports often show a contrast. Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline. Despite the delay, quality stayed high. Today you will learn to link two contrasting ideas with although, even though, despite and in spite of.
vocab: Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Even though the audit was tough, we passed it.
Despite the delay, quality stayed high.
In spite of the problem, the delivery was on time.
The audit was tough; however, we passed.
Despite the delay, we finished on time.
practice: We met the deadline ______ the parts arrived late.
although
We passed the audit ______ it was very tough.
even though
The quality stayed high ______ the delay.
despite
The delivery was on time ______ the earlier problem.
in spite of
The audit was tough; ______, we passed it.
however
Despite the ______, we finished the order on time.
delay
We shipped the units ______ a small non-conformity.
despite
The line kept running ______ the sensor failed.
even though

audio.title: The monthly quality summary
audio.text: This month brought some challenges, but the results were strong. Although the raw materials arrived late, the team still met the delivery deadline. Even though the ISO audit was demanding, we passed it without any major non-conformity. Despite a small defect in one panel, the equipment was shipped on time. In spite of the tight schedule, every inspection was completed. The month was hard; however, our quality stayed high.

readAloud: Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Even though the audit was tough, we passed it.
Despite the delay, quality stayed high.
In spite of the problem, the delivery was on time.
The inspection was hard; however, we found no major issues.
fill: ___ the parts arrived late, we met the deadline. (Although/Despite)
We passed ___ the audit was tough. (even though/in spite of)
We shipped on time ___ the small problem. (even though/in spite of)
___ we found a defect, we corrected it fast. (Although/Despite)
___ the bad weather, the field team finished the assembly. (Although/Despite)
The system worked ___ one sensor failed. (even though/in spite of)
We met the target ___ the tight schedule. (although/in spite of)
qa: Did you meet the deadline?
Yes, although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Was the audit difficult?
Yes, but even though it was tough, we passed it.
Did the delay affect quality?
No, despite the delay, quality stayed high.
Was the delivery on time?
Yes, in spite of the problem, it was on time.
Did the defect stop the shipment?
No, although we found a defect, we still shipped on time.

a.label: although / even though + frase
a.placeholder: Although we found a defect, we met the deadline

b.label: despite / in spite of + substantivo
b.placeholder: Despite the delay, quality stayed high

sentences: Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Even though the audit was tough, we passed it.
Despite the delay, quality stayed high.
In spite of the earlier problem, the delivery was on time.
Although we found a small defect, we corrected it quickly.
Despite the tight schedule, the team finished the assembly.
The system kept running even though one sensor failed.
We met the target in spite of the material shortage.
grammarPoint: Contraste. although e even though vêm antes de uma oração (sujeito + verbo): Although it rained, we worked. — Embora chovesse, trabalhamos. despite e in spite of vêm antes de um substantivo (ou verbo -ing): Despite the rain, we worked. — Apesar da chuva, trabalhamos. however (porém) liga duas frases, geralmente depois de ponto e vírgula.
deepDive: Cuidado com dois erros clássicos: 'despite of' não existe (é só 'despite'); e a expressão é 'in spite of' (com 'of'). Depois de despite / in spite of use substantivo, pronome ou verbo com -ing (Despite arriving late...). Para colocar uma oração completa depois de despite, use 'despite the fact that'. even though é mais enfático que although.
examples: Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Embora as peças tenham chegado atrasadas, cumprimos o prazo.
Even though the audit was tough, we passed it.
Mesmo que a auditoria tenha sido dura, passamos nela.
Despite the delay, quality stayed high.
Apesar do atraso, a qualidade se manteve alta.
In spite of the problem, the delivery was on time.
Apesar do problema, a entrega foi no prazo.
Although we found a defect, we corrected it fast.
Embora tenhamos encontrado um defeito, corrigimos rápido.
Despite the tight schedule, we finished the assembly.
Apesar do cronograma apertado, terminamos a montagem.
The audit was hard; however, we passed.
A auditoria foi difícil; porém, passamos.
We met the target in spite of the shortage.
Atingimos a meta apesar da falta de material.
mistakes: Despite the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Although the parts arrived late, we met the deadline.
Antes de uma oração (sujeito+verbo) use although, não despite.
Although the delay, quality stayed high.
Despite the delay, quality stayed high.
Antes de um substantivo (the delay) use despite.
Despite of the problem, we finished on time.
Despite the problem, we finished on time.
Despite não leva 'of'.
In spite the delay, we shipped on time.
In spite of the delay, we shipped on time.
A expressão é 'in spite of' (com of).
Even though the delay, we met the deadline.
Even though there was a delay, we met the deadline.
Even though pede uma oração completa (sujeito+verbo).
quick: ___ the parts arrived late, we met the deadline. (Although/Despite)
We passed ___ the audit was tough. (even though/in spite of)
We shipped ___ the small problem. (even though/in spite of)
___ we found a defect, we shipped on time. (Although/Despite)
